title: Lentil & Vegetable Pottage
description: A thick, cozy lentil-and-vegetable pottage made from inexpensive pantry staples and frozen vegetables.
substitutions: Use whatever frozen vegetables you have on hand.
Use water plus bouillon instead of broth.
Stir in a handful of spinach during the last 10 minutes if you have some to use up.

steps.text: Put the lentils, broth, vegetables, and seasonings in the slow cooker.
Cook until the lentils are very tender and the pottage is thick.
Taste, adjust the seasoning, and serve hot.

cookSteps.text: Add {{lentils}} rinsed lentils, {{broth}} broth, {{vegetables}} frozen mixed vegetables, onion powder, thyme, black pepper, and salt to the slow cooker. Stir well.
Cover and cook on HIGH for about 4 hours, until the lentils are very tender. You can also cook on LOW for 6–7 hours.
Stir well. If you want it thicker, mash a few spoonfuls of lentils against the side of the cooker and stir them back in. If it is too thick, add a splash of broth or water.
Taste and add more salt or pepper if needed. Serve hot.

storage: Refrigerate covered up to 4 days or freeze up to 3 months. Add a splash of broth or water when reheating if it thickens too much.

title: Split Pea & Carrot Pottage
description: A soft, thick split-pea pottage with carrots and gentle savory seasoning.
substitutions: Add a small amount of finely diced ham if you want a smoky version.
Use frozen peas and carrots in place of the sliced carrots for a different texture.
Use water plus bouillon instead of broth.

steps.text: Combine the split peas, broth, carrots, and seasonings.
Slow-cook until the peas collapse into a thick, creamy pottage.
Stir, season, and serve.

cookSteps.text: Put {{peas}} rinsed split peas, {{broth}} broth, {{carrots}} carrots, onion powder, thyme if using, black pepper, and salt into the slow cooker. Stir.
Cover and cook on HIGH for about 4 hours, or on LOW for 6–7 hours, until the peas are very soft and the mixture is thick.
Stir vigorously to make the pottage creamier. Add a little broth or water if you want it looser.
Taste and adjust salt and pepper before serving.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days or freeze up to 3 months. Split-pea pottage thickens as it sits, so loosen it with broth or water when reheating.

title: White Bean & Rosemary Pottage
description: A creamy-tasting white-bean pottage made without cream, with rosemary and simple pantry seasonings.

ingredients.item: frozen diced carrots or mixed vegetables

substitutions: Use cannellini, Great Northern, or navy beans.
Use thyme instead of rosemary.
Add a handful of spinach during the last 10 minutes.

steps.text: Combine the beans, broth, vegetables, and seasonings.
Cook until everything is hot and tender.
Mash some of the beans to thicken the pottage.

cookSteps.text: Add {{beans}} white beans, {{broth}} broth, {{vegetables}} vegetables, rosemary, onion powder, black pepper, and salt to the slow cooker. Stir.
Cover and cook on HIGH for about 2 hours, or on LOW for 3–4 hours, until the vegetables are tender and everything is hot.
Mash about one-third of the beans right in the cooker, then stir. This makes the broth thick and creamy without adding cream.
Taste and adjust the seasoning. Add a splash of broth if the pottage is thicker than you like.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days or freeze up to 3 months. Reheat gently with a splash of broth or water.

title: Chickpea, Tomato & Spinach Pottage
description: A bright, savory chickpea pottage with tomatoes and spinach that still feels hearty and filling.
substitutions: Use white beans instead of chickpeas.
Use frozen kale instead of spinach.
For a smoother texture, mash some of the chickpeas before serving.

steps.text: Add everything except the spinach to the slow cooker.
Cook until the flavors blend and the chickpeas are tender.
Stir in the spinach near the end and serve.

cookSteps.text: Add {{chickpeas}} chickpeas, {{tomatoes}} diced tomatoes, {{broth}} broth, garlic powder, Italian seasoning, black pepper, and salt to the slow cooker. Stir.
Cover and cook on HIGH for about 2 1/2 hours, or on LOW for 4–5 hours.
Stir in {{spinach}} frozen spinach. Cover and cook 10 more minutes, until the spinach is hot.
Mash a few chickpeas with the back of a spoon if you want a thicker pottage. Taste and adjust the seasoning.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days or freeze up to 3 months. Reheat until steaming hot.

title: Barley & Mushroom Pottage
description: A deeply savory barley-and-mushroom pottage with a pleasantly chewy texture and rich broth.
substitutions: Use extra mixed vegetables if you do not have mushrooms.
Use vegetable broth for a fully vegetarian version.
Add a spoonful of grated Parmesan at serving time if you want a richer finish.

steps.text: Combine the barley, broth, mushrooms, vegetables, and seasonings.
Slow-cook until the barley is tender and the broth has thickened.
Taste and serve.

cookSteps.text: Add {{barley}} rinsed pearl barley, {{broth}} broth, {{mushrooms}} mushrooms, {{vegetables}} mixed vegetables, onion powder, thyme, black pepper, and salt to the slow cooker. Stir.
Cover and cook on HIGH for about 4 hours, or on LOW for 6–7 hours, until the barley is tender.
Stir well. The barley should make the broth naturally thick and spoonable. Add a little broth or water if needed.
Taste and adjust the salt and pepper before serving.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days or freeze up to 3 months. Barley continues to absorb liquid, so add broth when reheating.

title: Potato & Cabbage Pottage
description: A humble, filling potato-and-cabbage pottage that cooks down soft and comforting.

ingredients.item: peeled potatoes, cut into small cubes

substitutions: Use frozen diced potatoes to save chopping time.
Add sliced carrots with the potatoes for a sweeter version.
Stir in a little milk at the end if you want a creamier pottage.

steps.text: Combine the potatoes, cabbage, broth, and seasonings.
Cook until the potatoes and cabbage are very tender.
Mash some of the potatoes to thicken the pottage.

cookSteps.text: Add {{potatoes}} potatoes, {{cabbage}} cabbage, {{broth}} broth, onion powder, thyme if using, black pepper, and salt to the slow cooker. Stir.
Cover and cook on HIGH for about 3 1/2 hours, or on LOW for 6 hours, until the potatoes are very tender.
Mash some of the potatoes directly in the cooker, leaving plenty of soft pieces intact. Stir until the broth becomes thicker.
Taste and adjust the seasoning. Add a splash of broth if you want it thinner.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days. This pottage can be frozen, though the potatoes may become slightly softer after thawing.

title: Sweet Potato & Red Lentil Pottage
description: A soft, naturally creamy red-lentil pottage with sweet potato and warm, mild seasoning.

ingredients.item: peeled sweet potato, cut into small cubes

substitutions: Use regular potatoes instead of sweet potatoes for a less sweet version.
Leave out the cumin for a very plain, gentle flavor.
Stir in frozen spinach during the last 10 minutes if desired.

steps.text: Combine the lentils, sweet potato, broth, and seasonings.
Cook until everything is very soft.
Stir until creamy and season to taste.

cookSteps.text: Add {{lentils}} rinsed red lentils, {{sweetPotato}} sweet potato, {{broth}} broth, onion powder, cumin if using, black pepper, and salt to the slow cooker. Stir.
Cover and cook on HIGH for about 3 hours, or on LOW for 5–6 hours, until the sweet potato is very soft and the lentils have broken down.
Stir well; the red lentils should make the pottage naturally creamy. Mash a few sweet-potato pieces if you want it even smoother.
Taste and adjust salt and pepper before serving.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days or freeze up to 3 months. Add broth or water when reheating if needed.

title: Creamy Corn & Potato Pottage
description: A mild corn-and-potato pottage finished with a little milk for a cozy, chowder-like texture.

ingredients.item: peeled potatoes, cut into small cubes

substitutions: Use canned corn, drained, instead of frozen corn.
Use unsweetened plain oat milk if you prefer a dairy-free version.
Add finely diced ham at the beginning if you want a ham-and-corn version.

steps.text: Cook the potatoes and corn in broth until very tender.
Mash some of the potatoes to thicken the pottage.
Stir in milk at the end and heat gently.

cookSteps.text: Add {{potatoes}} potatoes, {{corn}} corn, {{broth}} broth, onion powder, black pepper, and salt to the slow cooker. Stir.
Cover and cook on HIGH for about 3 1/2 hours, or on LOW for 6 hours, until the potatoes are very tender.
Mash about one-third of the potatoes in the cooker and stir to thicken the broth.
Stir in {{milk}} milk. Cover and heat for 10 more minutes, just until hot; do not let it boil hard.
Taste and adjust the salt and pepper. Serve hot.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days. Reheat gently, stirring often; add a splash of milk or broth if it becomes too thick.
